proposed.explanation: While classical principles influenced architecture, Tschumi's strategy was deconstructivist fragmentation, not harmonious proportion. Tschumi's design actively intervened with red metal follies and strategic landscape restructuring. Tschumi explicitly rejected unified harmony; this contradicts his approach. Tschumi rejected the unified, hierarchically organized park in favor of a disjunctive system where points (follies), lines (paths), and surfaces (programmed zones) operate according to different logics...productive tensions between contradictory systems could generate spatial richness and experiential complexity.'
